question_text: How does the General Property Form coordinate payment with another flood insurance policy, and how does the deductible affect when the policy begins to share the loss?
reference_answer: When a covered loss is also insured under another flood insurance policy not issued under the National Flood Insurance Act, the General Property Form generally pays its proportional share of the loss. If the other policy is written as excess insurance, the NFIP policy becomes primary. When another flood policy also applies, the NFIP policy is primary, subject to its own deductible, up to the amount of the other policy's deductible. After the other deductible has been reached, the NFIP policy participates in the loss according to its proportional share of the total insurance.
